title: get_session_id crashes on missing 'last_active' key instead of handling gracefully
description: In bridge.py's get_session_id(), after parsing the JSON file, the code accesses data['last_active'] without checking if the key exists. The except clause catches json.JSONDecodeError and KeyError — so a missing 'last_active' key will trigger KeyError, which deletes the session file. However, this is a silent data loss path: if a session file is written by a newer or older version of the code that uses a different schema, or if the file is partially written due to a crash during save_session_id(), the session is silently deleted rather than preserved or repaired. The except clause should distinguish between 'file is corrupt' (delete) and 'file has unexpected schema' (log and preserve).
acceptance_criteria: get_session_id uses .get() for all dict access with explicit handling for missing keys. Corrupt files are logged at WARNING level before deletion. Schema mismatches are logged but the file is preserved.

title: Race condition in auth state file read/write
description: auth.py's _load_state()/_save_state() read and write auth/sessions.json without any file locking. With concurrent_updates=True in the Telegram bot, multiple handler coroutines can call auth functions simultaneously from different threads (via run_in_executor). Two concurrent handlers could: (1) both read the file, (2) each modify their copy, (3) write back — last writer wins, silently dropping the other's changes. This can corrupt pending auth tokens, session state, or rate-limit data. The same issue exists with _load_totp_secrets/_save_totp_secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Auth state file operations use fcntl.flock() or equivalent to prevent concurrent read-modify-write corruption. Test with concurrent access simulated.

title: Bot token fallback chain has no timeout — pass-cli or security can hang indefinitely at startup
description: At module level, bridge.py runs subprocess.run() to call pass-cli and security (macOS Keychain) to retrieve the bot token. Neither call has a timeout parameter. If pass-cli hangs (e.g. waiting for GPG agent, network issue with Proton Pass), the bridge startup blocks indefinitely. The same issue exists in auth_server.py for the APPLE_SUBJECT_ALLOWLIST retrieval — two subprocess.run() calls with no timeout. Since these run at import time, the bridge never starts and launchd's KeepAlive will keep trying to restart it, creating a loop of hanging processes.
acceptance_criteria: All subprocess.run() calls for secret retrieval have a timeout (e.g. 10 seconds). On timeout, fall through to the next retrieval method. Log a warning when a retrieval method times out.

title: Bridge integration - gate messages behind auth
No health check or liveness probe beyond /ping
description: The bridge has no automated health monitoring. /ping only works if Adrien manually sends the command — it does not detect if the Telegram polling loop has silently stopped receiving messages, if the event loop is blocked, or if the bridge is alive but not processing. There is no external liveness check that could alert when the bridge is effectively dead. The launchd plist only restarts on non-zero exit — if the process hangs (e.g. event loop deadlock), launchd will not intervene. The stall detector only checks Claude subprocesses, not the bridge's own health.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge writes a heartbeat file (timestamp) every 60 seconds. External watchdog (cron or launchd) checks the heartbeat file age and restarts the bridge if it exceeds 5 minutes. Alternatively, bridge sends periodic self-ping via Telegram API.

title: Stall detector can send malformed notification if session_key format changes
description: In _stall_detector(), when a stalled process is killed, the code parses the session_key to extract chat_id and thread_id: 'parts = key.split("_", 1); chat_id = int(parts[0])'. This assumes session keys are always in the format 'chatid_threadid' or just 'chatid'. If the session_key format ever changes, or if a key from _active_procs is malformed, int(parts[0]) will raise ValueError, which is caught by the broad 'except Exception: pass' — silently swallowing the error and preventing the user from being notified about the stalled process kill. The notification is the user's only feedback that their process was killed.
acceptance_criteria: Session key parsing in stall detector uses a dedicated helper with explicit error handling. Failed notification attempt is logged at WARNING level, not silently swallowed.

title: No retry logic for Telegram API send failures
description: In _send_response(), when a Telegram send_message call fails, the exception is re-raised. The caller in handle_message catches it and calls _notify_delivery_failure (best-effort), but the original response is permanently lost. There is no retry with exponential backoff for transient Telegram API failures (429 rate limit, 503 server error, network timeout). For a bridge that is the sole communication channel, losing a response due to a transient API blip is unacceptable.

title: Auth server _fetch_apple_keys has no error handling for network failures
description: In auth_server.py, _fetch_apple_keys() calls resp.raise_for_status() but the exception propagates up to _verify_apple_id_token and then to apple_callback where it is caught by a broad 'except Exception'. However, if Apple's key server is temporarily down, the error message shown to the user is the raw exception text ('Connection refused', 'Timeout', etc.) — not a user-friendly message. Worse, the cache is only valid for 1 hour, so a brief Apple outage will block ALL authentications even though existing sessions are fine. There should be a stale-while-revalidate pattern: use cached keys even if they are slightly expired rather than failing hard.
acceptance_criteria: Apple key fetch uses stale-while-revalidate: if network fetch fails, use last-known-good keys (cached indefinitely). User sees a friendly error message on auth failure, not raw exception text.

title: Multimedia support via ProtonDrive shared folder
No graceful shutdown — active Claude processes orphaned on SIGTERM
description: When the bridge receives SIGTERM (from launchd shutdown or macOS restart), the Python process exits. run.sh traps SIGTERM and sends it to the bridge child, then exits 0. However, bridge.py has no signal handler — it relies on python-telegram-bot's run_polling() to handle shutdown. Active Claude subprocesses in _active_procs are NOT terminated on bridge shutdown. The run_claude function runs in a ThreadPoolExecutor, and the Popen processes have no cleanup hook. These child processes become orphans, continuing to run (and potentially making changes) after the bridge dies. On restart, the bridge has no way to know about these orphans.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge registers SIGTERM handler that terminates all active Claude processes in _active_procs and _remote_proc before exiting. Orphan processes are cleaned up.

title: Bridge: Telegram Conflict (409) errors logged 1,138 times — no single-instance guard
description:
Distillation pass over bridge.log surfaced 1,138 occurrences of:

```
telegram.error.Conflict: Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request; make sure that only one bot instance is running.
```

This is the same root cause as the 04-18 stargate outage: two processes simultaneously polling the Telegram getUpdates API on the same bot token. Telegram allows only one poller; the second gets 409 Conflict. The bridge keeps trying, logging each one, but never alerts or exits cleanly.

## Why
Restart sequences (manual, launchd, or self-restart after stall) don't reliably ensure the prior bridge process is fully terminated and has released the poller before the new one starts. Result: continuous low-level log spam during the overlap, plus the occasional outage when both refuse to back off.

## Acceptance
1. Pre-start: bridge checks for an existing instance (PID file, lockfile, or Telegram getMe with retry-on-409 backoff). If detected, either: (a) wait for it to exit with a sane timeout, then take over, or (b) exit cleanly with a log line explaining the situation.
2. Conflict errors during runtime should aggregate: log first occurrence, then a counter every N seconds rather than per-event spam.
3. Sustained Conflict storm (>5 min) should escalate as a self-heal trigger or notification, not silently roll forever.
4. Confirm log doesn't accumulate >100MB unrotated (separate issue but related).

## Source
~/Developer/claude-session-db/distill/22-workflow-primitives.md and 13-silent-loss-breadcrumbs.md
~/Developer/stargate/logs/bridge.log

## Discovered during
Conversation-archive distillation pass, 2026-04-21.

title: No audit trail for outbound Claude→Telegram responses; suspected MarkdownV2 render drops
description:
## Symptom

User reports receiving only fragments of Claude's response on phone (seeing e.g. "Both models landed" and "Heads up" but missing the body between them). Occurred 2026-04-22 ~08:44 on chat -1003884282041_472.

## What the bridge sees

- bridge.err shows a single sendMessage POST at 08:44:21 returning HTTP 200 OK.
- No MarkdownV2 parse-error fallback triggered (would have logged "MarkdownV2 send failed, falling back to plain").
- One 427-char chunk, under TELEGRAM_MSG_LIMIT (4096), single sendMessage.

From stargate's perspective the send was clean. From the user's perspective, content was lost. We have no way to reconcile because _send_response (bridge.py:429) does not persist the actual text or converted MarkdownV2.

## Hypothesized cause

telegramify_markdown produces questionable MarkdownV2 that some Telegram clients silently drop or mis-render:

1. Escaped special chars inside code spans. Example from the dropped message: ``\.pi`` — telegramify escaped the dot INSIDE the backtick span. MarkdownV2 spec says only backtick and backslash should be escaped inside code; escaping other chars is undefined behavior and clients differ on whether they render the backslash literal, drop the span, or partially render.
2. Unicode bullet U+29C1 (⦁) used for list items. Not consistently rendered on mobile Telegram.

Both would pass Telegram's server-side MarkdownV2 validator (hence 200 OK), but render partially on some clients — fully explains the "only saw the prose, not the bulleted list" symptom.

## Root problem: no audit trail

We cannot diagnose client-side render failures without knowing what we actually sent. Every future "I didn't see X" complaint becomes guesswork.

## Fix — primary (this bead)

Extend stargate/outbound.py — which already logs agent-originated notifications to outbound/<session>.jsonl — to also capture outbound responses from _send_response.

Each entry should include:
- ts (epoch float)
- session_key (chat_id[_thread_id])
- chunk_index (0-based within a single logical response)
- chunk_total
- raw_text (plain markdown, what Claude emitted)
- md_text (converted MarkdownV2, what Telegram actually received; null if fallback)
- parse_mode ("MarkdownV2" or "plain")
- http_status (or exception class on failure)

Implementation surface:
- Add `log_outbound_response(session_key, chunk_index, chunk_total, raw, md, parse_mode, status)` to stargate/outbound.py.
- Call it inside the retry loop of bridge._send_response after each successful send and on final failure.
- Add a test to tests/test_telegram_helpers.py.

Keeps the existing outbound.jsonl format (add a "source": "claude-response" discriminator vs the existing "banana"/agent sources).

## Fix — follow-up (separate bead later)

Pre-send MarkdownV2 sanity check: reject converted output that contains escape sequences inside code spans or unmatched entities, and fall back to plain text before Telegram sees it. Higher payoff, larger change, separate concern.

## Acceptance

- Every response sent to Telegram lands as one or more lines in outbound/<session_key>.jsonl with the fields above.
- `cat outbound/-1003884282041_472.jsonl | tail` shows the literal MarkdownV2 we sent for the last response.
- Test verifies both the happy path (MarkdownV2 send succeeds) and the fallback path (MarkdownV2 send fails → plain retry → logged with parse_mode="plain").
- No change to user-visible bridge behavior; purely additive.

title: Photo temp files accumulate if bridge crashes during photo processing
description: In handle_photo(), downloaded photos are saved to PHOTO_DIR (a tempdir subdirectory) and deleted in the finally block after processing. However, if the bridge crashes during photo processing (between download and the finally block), the photo file is never cleaned up. PHOTO_DIR is inside /tmp which macOS eventually cleans, but repeated crashes could accumulate files. More importantly, the photo directory is created with default permissions in the system temp dir — if multiple users or processes share /tmp, the photos could be readable by other processes. The photos may contain sensitive content sent via Telegram.

title: Error details from auth_server exposed to unauthenticated users in HTML
description:
In auth_server.py's apple_callback, when Apple token verification fails, the raw exception message is included in the HTML response: 'f"

Verification failed

{e}

"'. This leaks internal error details (stack traces, JWT validation errors, network error details) to unauthenticated users. The error object 'e' could contain server hostnames, file paths, or library version information that aids an attacker. Similarly, the Apple error parameter from the OAuth redirect is reflected directly in HTML: 'f"

Authentication failed

{error}

"' — this is a potential reflected XSS vector if the error parameter contains HTML/JavaScript.
acceptance_criteria: Error responses show generic user-friendly messages. Detailed error info is logged server-side only. Error parameter is HTML-escaped before rendering. No internal details leak to the client.

title: Session files use session_key directly in filename — path traversal risk
description: save_session_id() constructs the session file path as SESSION_DIR / f'{session_key}.json'. The session_key comes from _session_key(chat_id, thread_id) which concatenates chat_id and thread_id with an underscore. While Telegram chat IDs are normally numeric, the code does not validate this. If a crafted session_key containing path separators (e.g. '../../../etc/passwd') were somehow injected, it could write files outside SESSION_DIR. Similarly, save_pending() uses uuid.uuid4().hex[:12] which is safe, but the session_key is stored in the JSON content. The same pattern exists in chat_projects.json where session keys are used as JSON object keys.
acceptance_criteria: Session key construction validates that chat_id is numeric and thread_id is numeric or None. Filename construction uses a sanitization step that strips path separators.

title: Missing env var validation for critical configuration at startup
description: Several env vars are parsed at module level with no validation of the result. MAX_TIMEOUT, MAX_TURNS, MAX_WORKERS, AUTH_PORT are all parsed with int() from env vars — if they contain non-numeric values, the bridge crashes with an unhelpful ValueError traceback instead of a clear error message and non-zero exit. SESSION_EXPIRY has the same issue. CLAUDE_PATH is used without checking if the binary exists. WORKING_DIR is used without checking if the directory exists. AUTH_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT in auth.py has the same int() parse without validation. If any of these are misconfigured after a .env edit, the bridge crashes and the self-heal loop tries to fix Python code when the real problem is configuration.
acceptance_criteria: All env var parsing has try/except with clear error messages. Critical paths (CLAUDE_PATH, WORKING_DIR) are validated to exist at startup. Invalid config produces a human-readable error, not a traceback.

title: Unbounded message queue can exhaust memory
description: In handle_message(), when a session is processing, follow-up messages are appended to _queued_messages[key] with no upper bound. If Adrien sends many messages while a long Claude run is in progress (or if Claude hangs for 45 min until MAX_TIMEOUT), the queue grows without limit. While memory exhaustion is unlikely in practice, there is no feedback to the user that the queue is getting large, and no cap to prevent pathological cases. Additionally, queued messages are only in memory — if the bridge crashes, all queued messages are lost (only the initial pending message is persisted to disk).
acceptance_criteria: Queue has a max depth (e.g. 20 messages). Beyond the cap, user is told to wait. Queued messages are persisted to disk so they survive crashes.

title: Security: auth sessions.json and totp_secrets.json should have restrictive file permissions

These files contain auth state and TOTP secrets. They should be 0o600 (owner read/write only). Add chmod calls in _save_state and _save_totp_secrets, and add a startup check that warns if permissions are too open.
acceptance_criteria: auth/ files are 0o600 after write; startup logs warning if files are world-readable

title: Activity log grows without bound — no rotation or cleanup

Over months of operation, this file will grow to hundreds of MB or GB. The same issue exists for auth/auth_log.jsonl. Both files will eventually impact disk space and I/O performance. The bridge logs directory also has no rotation configured — bridge.log and bridge.err are written to by launchd with no size management.
acceptance_criteria: activity.jsonl and auth_log.jsonl are rotated (e.g. daily or at 10MB). Old logs are compressed or deleted after 30 days. Launchd logs have rotation configured.

title: Session timeout - auto-expire inactive sessions

title: Stargate /remote_control is tight — likely needs tmux or similar
description: Today /remote_control just spawns 'claude remote-control' as a Popen subprocess in the topic's project dir, captures the first 10s of stdout for the connection info, then leaves it running with a daemon drainer. That works but several rough edges: the user can't reattach if they lose the connection details, there's no way to see live output from the session beyond the initial capture, and the daemon drainer discards everything past the first 10s. If we want this to actually be useful for an interactive remote-control workflow we probably need to wrap it in tmux or screen so the session is reattachable / inspectable from any device, not just the moment Stargate started it. Aspirational — leave the basic Popen path in place until we redesign.

title: Self-heal CC session runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions on the full repo
description: In run.sh, the self-heal CC session launched after crash-loop detection uses --dangerously-skip-permissions with full repo access. If the crash was caused by a security issue (e.g. injected message content that exploits Claude), the self-heal session runs in the same compromised environment with elevated permissions. The self-heal prompt includes 'error_tail' which is the last 80 lines of bridge.err — if the error log contains attacker-controlled content (e.g. from a crafted Telegram message that made it into the log), this content is injected directly into the Claude prompt. The self-heal session also has no timeout — it could run indefinitely.
acceptance_criteria: Self-heal session has a timeout (e.g. 10 minutes). Error tail is sanitized before inclusion in the prompt. Consider running self-heal in a sandboxed environment or at least without --dangerously-skip-permissions.

title: Error handling: bridge startup should fail fast if BOT_TOKEN is empty

Currently the bridge starts and crashes only when it tries to connect. Add a startup check: if BOT_TOKEN is empty, print a clear error message and exit(1) before building the Application. Test: simulate empty BOT_TOKEN and verify sys.exit(1) is called with a meaningful message.
acceptance_criteria: Empty BOT_TOKEN → fast fail with clear error at startup, not a cryptic Telegram API error

title: Test: session auto-expires after SESSION_EXPIRY seconds of inactivity

title: Recursive retry in run_claude can stack overflow on persistent stale sessions
description: When run_claude detects a stale session (stderr contains 'No conversation found'), it calls clear_session() and then recursively calls itself: 'return run_claude(message, session_key)'. If the Claude CLI keeps returning 'No conversation found' for a different reason (bug, corrupt state), this creates infinite recursion until Python hits the recursion limit and crashes with a RecursionError. There is no recursion guard or retry count limit.
acceptance_criteria: Stale session retry uses an explicit retry counter (max 1 retry) instead of recursion. After the retry, if it still fails, return an error message to the user.

title: Pluggable backend support in stargate (Claude vs pi, per-topic)
description:
Today stargate's CLAUDE_PATH is a single global constant. The claude-pi-shim (in picurious/bin/claude-pi-shim) gives us cwd-based backend dispatch with no stargate changes — a good spike, but not the clean answer.

This bead tracks the Option 2 refactor: first-class backend concept per topic.

## Scope

- Introduce a 'backend' enum per-topic: 'claude' (default), 'pi', future 'aider' etc.
- bridge.run_claude() → bridge.run_agent(backend, ...) with per-backend command builder + parser.
- Per-backend flag whitelist (no-op for flags the backend doesn't understand).
- Per-topic /backend <name> command to switch.
- Per-backend quota-handoff policy (pi has no quota; skip forge handoff).
- Remove the shim's cwd-dispatch once this is live.

## Prereqs

- Spike via claude-pi-shim succeeds end-to-end in a real Telegram topic.
- Audit outbound-logging bead (CTB-80f) is in so we can diagnose backend-specific render issues.

## Out of scope

- Aider/other backends. Design must leave room, but only pi lands in this bead.
- UI changes beyond /backend command.

## Acceptance

- Can bind any topic to backend=pi via /backend pi, and messages route to pi without CLAUDE_PATH manipulation.
- Existing claude topics untouched.
- Tests cover per-backend command construction + output parsing.

title: ThreadPoolExecutor with 4 workers can exhaust under concurrent sessions
description: The bridge uses a ThreadPoolExecutor with MAX_WORKERS=4. Each Claude invocation blocks a thread for up to MAX_TIMEOUT=2700 seconds (45 min). With concurrent_updates=True, multiple forum topics can receive messages simultaneously. If 4 topics all have active Claude processes, the executor is fully saturated — the 5th topic's message will block in run_in_executor until a thread frees up. The user sees typing indicators but gets no response (or a very delayed one). There is no feedback to the user that all workers are busy, no queuing notification, and no monitoring of executor saturation. The stall detector may kill one eventually, but only after 10 min of idle CPU.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge monitors executor saturation. When all workers are busy, user receives immediate feedback instead of silent waiting. Consider dynamic worker pool sizing or at minimum logging when saturation occurs.

title: Remote control stdout reader blocks executor thread indefinitely if process hangs
description: In cmd_remote_control(), _read_initial_output() reads from the remote-control process stdout with a 10-second deadline. However, after those 10 seconds, the function returns and the process continues running. Its stdout pipe is never read again. If the remote-control process produces substantial output, stdout fills up the OS pipe buffer (typically 64KB on macOS). Once full, the process blocks on write, effectively hanging. Additionally, the remote-control process stdout is never drained or closed after the initial read, so stdout remains piped but unread for the lifetime of the process.
acceptance_criteria: After initial output capture, either: (a) redirect stdout to /dev/null, (b) start a background thread to drain stdout, or (c) don't pipe stdout at all after initial capture.

acceptance_criteria: chat_projects.json read-modify-write operations use file locking. Alternatively, use a single-writer pattern via asyncio queue.

title: Pending message replay silently drops errors — no notification to user
description: In replay_pending(), if run_claude raises an exception during replay, the error is caught and 'response = f"Error: {e}"' is sent to the user. However, if the Telegram send itself fails (e.g. during a brief Telegram outage at startup), the exception propagates up and the remaining pending messages are never replayed. The pending file was already deleted before processing (to prevent crash loops), so the message is permanently lost. Additionally, the replay loop processes messages sequentially with no timeout — a single slow Claude invocation could block all other pending replays.
acceptance_criteria: replay_pending catches send failures per-message and continues with remaining messages. Failed replays are re-saved to the pending directory. Each replay has an individual timeout.

title: Parse Telegram messages split across multiple updates as one logical message
description:
When a user sends a very long message in Telegram, the client splits it into multiple separate Telegram messages (typically two). Today the bridge processes each split fragment as its own message — either invoking Claude twice or creating a queued/batched second turn instead of treating them as a single user turn.

Repro: Send a message long enough that Telegram splits it (>~4096 chars in the client). Observe that the bridge sees two messages, not one logical message.

Expected: Coalesce split-message fragments from the same user within a short window (debounce / continuation detection) so Claude sees the full intended prompt as a single turn.

Implementation notes:
- Telegram does not flag the split — both arrive as independent Update objects with no continuation marker.
- Heuristic: same chat_id + thread_id + sender, arriving within ~1-2s, where the previous message ends mid-sentence (no terminal punctuation) or is exactly at the client split boundary.
- Existing pending-message debounce in patchbay/sessions.py is the natural place to extend.
- Care needed not to wrongly merge two genuinely distinct rapid-fire messages.

title: Long messages split into two arrive as separate Telegram updates and aren't parsed/joined
description: When Telegram splits a very long incoming message into two updates (Telegram client-side ~4096 char split), the bridge currently treats them as two independent messages. They should be detected and joined before being sent to the harness, or at minimum the queued/batched delivery should reconstruct them in order. Reported via Telegram on 2026-05-07. Likely arrives as a queued message because the second part lands while the first is still being processed.

title: Document and ship Python version pinning pattern
description:
Patchbay Relay's design assumes a pinned Python version on the host so Homebrew can never silently change the binary path and revoke TCC permissions. We need to ship this as a real Patchbay Relay feature, not a private deployment habit.

Two artifacts:

1. Doc in repo: 'docs/python-version-management.md' or similar. Describes:
   - Why Python pinning matters on macOS (TCC binary-path coupling).
   - How to pin via Homebrew (brew pin python@3.13 etc.).
   - The recommended upgrade workflow: watch upstream releases, scan changelogs, add to ignore list if not worth the cost, schedule a planned upgrade if it is.

2. Optional CLI utility: 'patchbay python-check' (or a small script under scripts/) that:
   - Reads currently pinned version from a config/environment.
   - Fetches latest Python release feed.
   - Scans changelog text for keywords (security, CVE, fixes, plus user-configured 'features I care about').
   - Persists an ignore list of dismissed releases.
   - Prints a recommendation: 'upgrade now' with rationale, or 'safe to ignore' silently.

Doc alone is enough for the launch. CLI is optional polish.

Blog post (synodic.co/patchbay/) describes this design in present tense. Must be true before publish, otherwise post is vapor.
